title: Cleaning the battered cornet and playing The Palms at 17
summary: How he repaired and polished a patched horn, then played The Palms at 17 after a coaching scare.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Oh, but if you know, stare behind that little coronet. Yeah. Someone gave him that little horn, and he had holes in him, you know, and he stopped him up with gum, and the water valve was broke. And he took a piece of carc, and he cut it to fit. And it didn't stay down. He took a rubber band, and he wrapped around there. And they had something else, again, he had to put on it. I just remember now. But nevertheless, he would, whenever he had to clean it, he'd get those BB shots, you know what they call them? Oh, yeah. The little lead pellets. And he'd fill that up, and then he'd have soap water, and just shake that in there until he cleaned it out, and take every valve out. He'd almost stay there half a day, and then he'd have his pencil there, and walk in the valve, and he'd take them out and put the string back, you know?
Oh, yeah. So when you got them mixed up.

Then when he'd take that out, it was so green in there that he had a little brush, and he'd clean that out with the brush. Then when he'd get through with that, then he'd get some perpetua. The horn was so dirty looking, you know, so brassy. He'd make a paste with that, and he'd put it on the horn, and he'd let it dry. Then he'd start to polish, get a rag, and polish, and polish, until he'd get it just the way he wanted. What was that preparation again? Perpato.
Some people use that to clean their teeth with, don't they? My mother used it.

Years ago, that's all he used to do. And how would you put it on that face? Perpato. And then the funny part of it, all stopped up like that, he would play it. He'd go on the job with that. Now you see here, I told you all that he played Night and Day at the Globes Hall, but my mother said it was the Palms. Yeah, he played the Palms. It was the Palms.
Night and Day came out later, I believe, anyway.
Night and Day would have come out later than that, I believe. But the Palms, that old French piece.

And this old lady there, she was so worried, when he left, he says, I'm going to say a class for you, because you don't know the grace note that you have in that piece, and you're going to make a fool of yourself. She said, why do you want to do that? Why don't you tell them you're sick? She said, I'm gone. And he said it all the way through. He never made one mistake.
